title: General Technology
description: 36 original questions covering computing, networking, cybersecurity, AI, software, and smart homes (Multiple Choice & Free-Text).
author: QuizRooms

questions.prompt: What does the acronym CPU stand for in computing?
questions.explanation: The CPU executes instructions that make up computer programs.

questions.prompt: Which markup language defines the structure of web pages?
questions.explanation: HTML stands for HyperText Markup Language.

questions.prompt: What does Wi-Fi allow devices to do without physical cables?
choices: Connect to a wireless local network
questions.answer: Connect to a wireless local network
questions.explanation: Wi-Fi uses radio waves to connect devices to a local area network.

questions.prompt: Which unit equals 1,024 bytes in traditional binary computing?
questions.explanation: A binary kilobyte (kibibyte) consists of 1,024 bytes.

questions.prompt: What does URL stand for?
questions.explanation: A URL specifies the web address of a resource on the Internet.

questions.prompt: Which company originally created the Android mobile operating system before Google acquired it?
questions.explanation: Andy Rubin and colleagues founded Android Inc. in 2003 before Google bought it in 2005.

questions.prompt: What is the name of the small glowing picture element that makes up a digital screen?
questions.explanation: Pixel is short for 'picture element'.

questions.prompt: Which keyboard shortcut commonly copies selected text on Windows and Linux?
questions.explanation: Ctrl+C copies, while Ctrl+V pastes and Ctrl+X cuts.

questions.prompt: What type of software protects a computer network by filtering incoming and outgoing traffic?
questions.explanation: A firewall enforces security rules on network traffic.

questions.prompt: Which hardware component stores active working data temporarily while a computer is powered on?
questions.explanation: RAM is volatile high-speed memory cleared when power is turned off.

questions.prompt: What does PDF stand for?
questions.explanation: Adobe introduced PDF in 1993 for consistent document rendering.

questions.prompt: Which open-source home automation platform runs locally to control smart devices?
questions.explanation: Home Assistant focuses on local control and privacy for smart homes.

questions.prompt: Which protocol adds TLS encryption on top of standard web browsing?
questions.explanation: HTTPS encrypts HTTP traffic using Transport Layer Security (TLS).

questions.prompt: What does DNS translate human-readable domain names into?
questions.explanation: The Domain Name System resolves names like example.com to numerical IP addresses.

questions.prompt: Which distributed version control system was created by Linus Torvalds in 2005?
questions.explanation: Git was originally built to manage Linux kernel development.

questions.prompt: What is the standard default TCP port number for HTTPS traffic?
questions.explanation: Port 443 is used for encrypted HTTPS, whereas port 80 is plain HTTP.

questions.prompt: Which wireless mesh protocol is widely used by low-power smart home sensors and bulbs on 2.4 GHz?
questions.explanation: Zigbee enables low-power mesh networking for IoT devices.

questions.prompt: What does SSD stand for in modern computer storage?
questions.explanation: SSDs use flash memory with no moving spinning platters.

questions.prompt: In databases, what does SQL stand for?
questions.explanation: SQL is used to query and manage relational databases.

questions.prompt: Which lightweight publish-subscribe messaging protocol is a cornerstone of IoT and smart home telemetry?
questions.explanation: MQTT uses a broker and topics for low-bandwidth IoT messaging.

questions.prompt: What does API stand for in software engineering?
questions.explanation: An API defines how software components communicate with one another.

questions.prompt: Which computer scientist invented the World Wide Web in 1989 while at CERN?
questions.explanation: Tim Berners-Lee created HTTP, HTML, and the first web browser.

questions.prompt: Which color model do digital monitors use to mix light?
questions.explanation: Screens emit additive Red, Green, and Blue light; printers use subtractive CMYK.

questions.prompt: What does JSON stand for?
questions.explanation: JSON is a lightweight text format for structured data exchange.

questions.prompt: Which HTTP status code indicates that a client has sent too many requests in a given amount of time?
questions.explanation: HTTP 429 Too Many Requests is used for rate limiting.

questions.prompt: What is the name of the consensus-free cryptographic hash family that includes SHA-256?
questions.explanation: SHA-256 belongs to the SHA-2 family published by NIST.

questions.prompt: Which layer of the OSI model handles logical addressing and packet routing (such as IP)?
questions.explanation: Layer 3 (Network) routes packets across interconnected networks.

questions.prompt: What technique lets a single CPU core execute instructions out of program order to reduce pipeline stalls?
questions.explanation: Modern superscalar CPUs reorder independent instructions dynamically.

questions.prompt: Which Linux kernel feature isolates process trees, networks, and mount points to power containers?
questions.explanation: Namespaces combined with cgroups form the foundation of Linux containers.

questions.prompt: In public-key cryptography, which key is used to verify a digital signature?
questions.explanation: The signer signs with their private key, and anyone can verify with the public key.

questions.prompt: What does ACID stand for in relational database transactions?
questions.explanation: ACID properties guarantee reliable database transactions.

questions.prompt: Which algorithm is famously used to find the shortest path in a weighted graph with non-negative edges?
questions.explanation: Edsger Dijkstra published his shortest-path algorithm in 1959.

questions.prompt: What is the maximum number of host addresses in a standard IPv4 /24 subnet (excluding network and broadcast)?
questions.explanation: A /24 subnet has 256 total addresses minus the network and broadcast addresses = 254.

questions.prompt: Which smart-home connectivity standard launched in 2022 operates over IPv6 using Thread and Wi-Fi?
questions.explanation: Matter unifies local smart-home interoperability across ecosystems over IPv6.

questions.prompt: What does CIDR stand for in IP networking?
questions.explanation: CIDR replaced rigid classful IP addressing with flexible prefix lengths like /24.

questions.prompt: Which data structure provides average O(1) key-value lookup using a hash function?
questions.explanation: Hash tables map keys through a hash function to array buckets for constant-time average lookup.
